1. High — the `findings_decline` detector can both fire on the wrong window and clear itself without real recovery.

**FIND:** Location: [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/dynamic_management.py), `DetectorHealthMonitor.__init__()` and `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_round()`, Check 4.  
The code says “declining for 3 rounds”, but it waits for 4 samples, then only inspects the last 3 (`recent_3`). That means it can diagnose a 3-round decline when there were only 2 downward steps in the current 4-round span. Example: `[5, 12, 10, 8]` triggers today because it inspects `[12, 10, 8]`, even though `5 -> 12` was an increase. The same block also clears the pathology on a flat plateau because it compares only the current short window. After a real decline like `[20, 14, 10, 8]`, three flat rounds `[8, 8, 8]` satisfy `recent_3[-1] >= recent_3[0]`, so the detector marks the issue resolved even though findings never recovered to the pre-decline level of `20`.
